comments.note: ShowInExplorer uses ArgumentList.Add($"/select,{filePath}") as a single entry — the plan explicitly warns against splitting into two entries (/select, and filePath) because explorer.exe treats the ArgumentList as space-separated tokens and cannot parse them separately. The single-entry form is the only correct approach.

WindowsFileLauncherService is not unit-tested (Process.Start calls cannot easily be intercepted without an IProcessLauncherService abstraction). The security fix is correct at the call-site level, but a future enhancement could introduce an abstraction layer to enable unit testing of the launch logic.

summary: Reviewed 2 files (WindowsFileLauncherService.cs, constraints.md). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 1 Low (Process.Start result silently discarded — not exploitable). Security sign-off: PASS. The core A03 argument injection vulnerability has been correctly remediated via ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList. The ShowInExplorer single-entry interpolation pattern ($\"/select,{filePath}\") is architecturally sound — this is the required format for explorer.exe's /select switch and the single ArgumentList entry prevents all OS-level argument splitting.

comments.note: [PASS] All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed against WindowsFileLauncherService.cs and constraints.md. No Critical or High findings. The A03 (Injection) risk from Arguments= string concatenation is fully remediated by ArgumentList.Add(). The ShowInExplorer single-entry form ($"/select,{filePath}") correctly fuses the switch and path into one atomic argument — splitting them would break explorer.exe selection behavior. All other OWASP categories (A01–A02, A04–A10) are not implicated by these changes.

[Low] A09 — Security Logging: Process.Start() return value is discarded (via `_ = Process.Start(psi)`) in both OpenFolder and ShowInExplorer. If explorer.exe fails to launch (e.g., access denied, or very rare OS-level issue), the failure is silently swallowed — no exception surface, no audit log entry. Not exploitable, but an operational gap. Remediation: wrap in a try/catch or log the null-return case (Process.Start returns null when UseShellExecute=true and the launch succeeds but cannot be tracked). File: src/VideoIndexer.App/Services/WindowsFileLauncherService.cs lines 19, 31.

comments.note: UseShellExecute = true combined with ArgumentList is the correct pattern here. PasteArguments.AppendArgument properly escapes each entry into a quoted Arguments string before ShellExecuteEx is called. Paths with spaces are handled safely.

The _ = Process.Start(psi) discard pattern is intentional and avoids CS4014 warnings. The Security Auditor noted the silent-failure risk (Low) — acceptable given this is a UI convenience operation where the user directly observes the outcome.
